key_insight: Accounting for temperature-dependent water properties through transformed mean profiles predicts turbulent channel friction and heat transfer within 2% of DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve water-cooling and heating calculations where constant-property assumptions misestimate flow resistance and heat transfer.
method: Run direct numerical simulations of heated and cooled water channel flow with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity.
Derive integral profile transformations from mean momentum and energy balances, with DNS-calibrated turbulence corrections.
Invert the transformations to predict friction and heat transfer, and test the corrections in the Spalart–Allmaras model.
evidence_signal: Across wall temperatures of 277–360 K and wall Prandtl numbers of 2–12, friction shifts by −39% to +32% relative to constant-property flow, while empirical correlations deviate from DNS by up to 26%.
watch_item: Corrections are calibrated on channel-flow DNS; accuracy weakens at the lowest Reynolds numbers, and transfer to other geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
